procedure: Quantities as printed in the source. Weigh about 1 gram of salicylic acid on weighing paper and place it in a 125-mL Erlenmeyer flask. In the hood, measure out 3.0 mL of acetic anhydride and add it to the flask. Add 3 drops of concentrated (85%) phosphoric acid. Heat in a boiling water bath at 100 C, stirring gently, and time the reaction for 15 minutes once the bath is boiling. After the 15 minutes add 1 mL of deionised water to hydrolyse the excess acetic anhydride. Remove the flask from the bath, add 9-10 mL of deionised water, swirl and let it cool. When crystals appear, ice-chill the flask for 10 minutes; if no crystals form, scratch the flask wall with a glass rod. Collect by vacuum filtration on a Buchner funnel, rinse with two chilled 3-mL portions of water and leave under vacuum for several minutes. To purify, dissolve the crude product in 4 mL of warm ethanol, remove from the heat, add 13 mL of cold water, ice-chill, collect by vacuum filtration and dry. The source states no yield - students determine it - so none is recorded here. Transcribed from the published procedure; the page is CC BY-SA at the URL in the citation.
